scope: SCOPED: atomic IPv4 datagram definition, arbitrary sender Identification and receiver ignoring Identification in the unfragmented IPv4 codec/quoted-header decoder. Updates RFC791 and RFC1122 Identification semantics. No full-document or full IPv4 host conformance: non-atomic datagrams, fragmentation/reassembly, non-atomic ID allocation/rate limits, forwarding, NAT and tunnel behavior are outside this inventory.

paragraphs.reason: Encoder emits exactly DF=1, MF=0 and zero fragment offset. Assertions inspect all 16 flag/offset bits, not just DF.

paragraphs.quote: The IPv4 ID field MUST NOT be used for purposes other than fragmentation and reassembly.
paragraphs.reason: In the selected unfragmented codec, no packet metadata, option handling or payload result depends on ID. Checksum-correct distinct-ID packets have equal parse and quote results; the Host reassembly engine (crates/stacks/ntcp-host/src/reassembly.rs) uses ID only in the non-atomic fragment key (source, destination, protocol, ID), and atomic datagrams bypass it. The Host allocator issues identifiers only for non-atomic datagrams (source fragments, DF-clear IP_PMTUDISC_DONT TCP packets and the DF-clear packets of an owner-disabled IPv4 route or path), and ICMP correlation never uses ID: ledger evidence of source fragments records none, and a quoted fragment correlates only by addresses, protocol, header and packet lengths, offset, MF and recorded data octets (Host dispatch tests correlate a renumbered quote of a later fragment and reject near misses carrying the original ID).

paragraphs.quote: Originating sources MAY set the IPv4 ID field of atomic datagrams to any value.
paragraphs.reason: The selected sender chooses zero for every atomic datagram, including different payloads; no per-flow ID uniqueness mechanism is needed or claimed.

paragraphs.quote: All devices that examine IPv4 headers MUST ignore the IPv4 ID field of atomic datagrams.
paragraphs.reason: Both live and quoted-header decoders ignore ID semantically while still verifying the header checksum. The test reseals the checksum for multiple ID values and compares every exposed field, options and payload.

paragraphs.quote: Sources emitting non-atomic datagrams MUST NOT repeat IPv4 ID values within one MDL for a given source address/destination address/protocol tuple.
paragraphs.reason: Context row, kept outside this inventory's atomic-datagram scope (non-atomic datagrams and their Identification allocation are excluded from it). T13's Host IdentifierAllocator (crates/stacks/ntcp-host/src/ident.rs) implements the rule for every non-atomic datagram the Host originates (source fragments of Host UDP and Echo Replies (a reply to a source-routed Echo Request takes the reversed, policy-authorized return route, registers no adjunct demand and is never sized by an adjunct-confirmed bound), DF-clear IP_PMTUDISC_DONT TCP packets and the DF-clear packets of an owner-disabled IPv4 route or path): IPv4 values are unique per (source, destination, protocol) across flows, routes and DSCP within a configured MDL (default 120 seconds, an operational estimate, not a guaranteed network maximum), leases are held for the whole MDL, never evicted and survive address, route and Host replacement, a new Host context either takes over the allocator or waits a full MDL, and the ceiling of 65536 non-atomic datagrams per tuple per MDL is explicit backpressure before any submission. The structural fragment encoder still takes its Identification from its caller.
